subject: Customer Success Operations RFP: TAM coverage, on-call handoffs, and incident comms
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@atlasbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasbank.com
Date: 2025-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP Appendix: CS/TAM operations questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to our RFP appendix focused on Customer Success operations. Our procurement and SRE teams want a concise set of answers to the following items so we can evaluate operational fit:

1) TAM coverage model: primary hours, escalation tiers, escalation contact times (phone vs email), and how handoffs work across timezones.
2) On-call handoff protocol: who owns incident routing, how is knowledge transferred for active incidents, and what docs or runbooks are provided?
3) Support hours and SLAs: committed hours (business vs 24x7), target response and resolution times by severity, and SLA credits/remediation process.
4) Incident communications: templates for customer notifications, expected cadence (initial, updates, resolution), and audit logging for communications.
5) Security/compliance evidentiary items: SOC 2 scope for support access, logging retention for audit, and whether we can get a redacted incident timeline example.

Would you please provide a single PDF or XLS with answers and any sample playbook pages? We are on a tight timeline and would like your response by EOD Aug 19 PST.

Best,
Julia Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Atlas Bank

Julia — please find our consolidated response attached and answers inline below. We also uploaded supporting artifacts to the HubSpot record and included a DocuSign stub for our standard SOW should you want to proceed quickly. Attachments: CS-Engagement-Playbook_v1.pdf, redwood_sla_matrix_2025.xlsx

Inline summary (short answers):

1) TAM coverage model
- Named TAMs: Yes — you will receive a named TAM during onboarding and the same TAM will be primary for the first 90 days of production. Post-90 days the TAM remains assigned for renewal/expansion discussions; a secondary on-call TAM rotates for operational coverage.
- Primary contact hours: 08:00–18:00 local business days for your prioritized TAM. For urgent operational issues outside those hours we provide a 24x7 critical incident path via our on-call rotation.
- Escalation tiers: Tier 1 (TAM / CS engineer), Tier 2 (Platform on-call), Tier 3 (SRE & Eng on-call). Phone escalation is supported for P0/P1 incidents; email/SMS for lower severities.

2) On-call handoff protocol
- Handoffs use a standardized checklist in the runbook (attached) and a Slack-secured channel for real-time context. Handoff steps: 1) active incident summary, 2) last-known mitigation steps, 3) open diagnostics (links to traces/logs), 4) next action owner.
- Example sequence for EU P1 at 02:00 UTC (redacted timeline included in the PDF):
  * 02:00 UTC — Monitoring alert triggers; platform on-call triages within 5–10 mins.
  * 02:10 UTC — TAM notified and posted initial customer-facing message.
  * 02:25 UTC — Escalated to SRE on-call; remediation plan proposed.
  * 03:00 UTC — Customer update with mitigation and ETA.
  * Handoffs are recorded in the incident timeline and retained per retention policy.

3) Support hours and SLAs
- Coverage: Business-hours TAM + 24x7 critical incident routing.
- Response targets (examples): P0 initial response < 15 mins, P1 < 1 hour, P2 < 4 hours, P3 < 24 hours.
- SLA credits: defined in SLA matrix (attached) with credit tiers tied to monthly uptime percentages; remediation requests processed via support portal and validated by Customer Success.

4) Incident communications
- Templates: initial notification, hourly update, and resolution summary templates included in the playbook PDF.
- Cadence: initial within response SLA, then updates at least hourly for P0/P1 until mitigation, and a final RCA/resolution within 72 hours or as mutually agreed.
- Audit logs: all customer-facing comms and internal handoff notes stored in our incident tracking system with immutable timestamps.

5) Security/compliance evidentiary items
- SOC 2: We provided a redacted control matrix excerpt in the PDF and contact points for control owners (redacted emails).
- Log retention: incident logs and communications retained for 3 years by default; configurable per contract.
- Redacted timeline: included in the playbook PDF — no PII, timestamps and roles only.

Other items:
- We included a sample runbook page describing on-call rotation, required contact methods, and escalation phone numbers (redacted).
- HubSpot record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ATB-0892 contains the ticket bundle, playbook, and SLA matrix.
- DocuSign: https://docusign.net/DocuSign/example-signature-link (SOW stub).

Would you like us to present these artifacts in a 30-minute ops-level walk-through tomorrow at 10:00 AM PST? If so, I will send a calendar invite and invite our Sr. SRE (Marissa) and Rachel from Compliance.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Regards,
